summary: Verified against the real PR branch (worker/task-20260727-122935-timesheet-budget-vs-actual, PR #597) rather than trusting the self-report: all 3 claimed fixes are real and correct. The roster-inclusion fix correctly seeds designerStatusByUser from the passed roster before falling back to entries, so a budgeted-but-entryless designer now resolves a real active/inactive status instead of being dropped from byDesignerStatus (confirmed by 3 new targeted unit tests). The N+1 fix is real: resolvePmsBillableRatePure genuinely exists in pms-time-service.ts (verified by reading the blob directly on the PR branch, since it predates this fix commit and wasn't in the diff itself) and designerTimesheetReport now fetches pmsBillableRates once upfront instead of calling the DB-backed resolveBillableRate per time entry. The response-shape fix (projectScoped/orgWide split) is a technically breaking API change, but I confirmed via git grep across the entire PR-branch tree that designerTimesheetReport has zero real callers anywhere (no API route, no UI page, only its own test file), so there is no actual consumer to break -- the PR's own claim on this point checks out. Schema field usage (pmsBudgetLineItems.userId/amount, pmsBudgets.projectId, pmsTimeEntries.spentOn/activityType, users.isActive) all match the real schema.ts definitions. Independently confirmed via `gh pr checks 597`: Build, Type Check, Unit Tests, Lint, E2E, Guardrail Presence, Terminology Guardrail, Asset Registry Coverage, Secret Scanning, and Security Pattern Check are all real passes on this exact head commit -- only the Mandatory Audit Check (expected, awaiting this review) and a Vercel preview (infra rate-limit, unrelated to code) are red. The diff is purely additive (new exported types/functions, new tests, no schema/migration/auth/workflow changes), correctly tier1.
issues: designerTimesheetReport() now fetches the full org's time entries, budget line items, users, and projects on every call (in addition to the already project-scoped byUser query), trading the old per-entry N+1 for an org-wide table scan per report call -- fine at current scale and since the report has no live route yet, but worth revisiting before wiring this into a real endpoint for large orgs.

A pms_budget_line_items row whose userId references a user not present in the org's users table (orphaned/deleted user) would still be excluded from byDesignerStatus while counting toward overallBudget, i.e. a residual, narrower version of the same undercount class -- edge case, not the audited bug, not blocking.
